label: Знать
description: A full conjugation deck for знать: present persons, past, future, and common knowledge contexts.

missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: First-person singular present. 1. 'Знаю' is the я-form of знать. 2. 'Точно' adds certainty. 3. 'Правильный ответ' is the accusative object — a clean everyday statement of confident knowledge.

Strategic focus: Second-person singular present. 1. 'Знаешь' is the ты-form of знать. 2. 'Хорошо' modifies the verb. 3. 'Дорогу домой' is the accusative object — a practical sentence about knowing the way.
Strategic focus: Third-person singular present. 1. 'Знает' is the он/она-form of знать. 2. 'Думает, что' frames the clause. 3. 'Всё' is the emphatic object — a common claim of total knowledge.
Strategic focus: Third-person singular present. 1. 'Знает' is the он/она-form of знать. 2. 'Меня' is the accusative pronoun object. 3. 'Лично' reinforces personal acquaintance.
Strategic focus: First-person plural present. 1. 'Знаем' is the мы-form of знать. 2. 'Все' is the subject quantifier. 3. 'Горькую правду' is the accusative object — a weighty collective assertion.
Strategic focus: Second-person plural present. 1. 'Знаете' is the polite or plural вы-form. 2. 'Этот город' is the accusative object. 3. Framed as a practical question about a place.

Strategic focus: Third-person plural present. 1. 'Знают' is the они-form of знать. 2. 'Свободно' means fluently. 3. 'Русский язык' is the accusative object — a common sentence about knowing a language.
Strategic focus: First-person singular negation. 1. 'Не знаю' negates the я-form of знать. 2. 'Этого' takes the genitive under negation. 3. One of the most high-value everyday phrases in Russian.

Strategic focus: Negated third-person singular. 1. 'Не знает' is the он/она-form negated. 2. 'Никто' forms the required double negative. 3. 'Этого' is genitive under negation — a natural idiomatic statement.
Strategic focus: Masculine past tense. 1. 'Знал' is the masculine past of знать. 2. 'Давно' sets the time frame. 3. 'Это секрет' is the object — a simple past statement of prior knowledge.
Strategic focus: Feminine past tense. 1. 'Знала' is the feminine past of знать. 2. 'Уже' marks completion. 3. 'Его имя' is the accusative object — a natural past-tense sentence.
Strategic focus: Neuter past tense. 1. 'Знало' is the neuter past of знать, agreeing with neuter 'сердце'. 2. 'Всю правду' is the accusative object. 3. Drills rare but required neuter agreement.
Strategic focus: Plural past tense. 1. 'Знали' is the plural past of знать. 2. 'Меня' is the accusative pronoun. 3. 'Раньше' sets the past frame — a common statement of former acquaintance.
Strategic focus: First-person imperfective future. 1. 'Буду' is the future auxiliary. 2. 'Знать' stays in the infinitive. 3. 'Скоро' and 'всё' fill out the compound imperfective future.

Strategic focus: First-person plural imperfective future. 1. 'Будем' is the мы-form auxiliary. 2. 'Знать' remains the infinitive. 3. 'Результат' is the object — reinforces the compound future pattern.
Strategic focus: Perfective future of узнать. 1. 'Узнаю' is the я-form meaning 'will find out'. 2. 'Всю правду' is the accusative object. 3. Contrasts perfective узнать with imperfective знать.
Strategic focus: Perfective future of узнать. 1. 'Узнаешь' is the ты-form, 'will find out'. 2. 'Точный ответ' is the accusative object. 3. Reinforces the perfective find-out meaning.
Strategic focus: Singular imperative. 1. 'Знай' is the informal command form of знать. 2. 'Своё место' is a fixed idiomatic object. 3. 'Молодой человек' is a vivid vocative address.
Strategic focus: Plural imperative. 1. 'Знайте' is the polite or plural command form. 2. 'Это' is the neuter object. 3. 'Раз и навсегда' is a firm idiomatic adverbial — a direct instruction.

Strategic focus: First-person singular with prepositional clause. 1. 'Знаю' is the я-form of знать. 2. 'Об этом' uses the prepositional case after об. 3. 'Давно' sets the time — a common knowledge-about construction.
Strategic focus: First-person plural with reciprocal object. 1. 'Знаем' is the мы-form of знать. 2. 'Друг друга' is the fixed reciprocal phrase. 3. 'Давно' deepens the mutual acquaintance.
